 ORDER
With the consent of learned counsel for the parties, the matter is finally heard.

By this petition preferred under Article 227 of the Constitution of Ind ia, the petitioner/plaintiff has challenged the order passed by the appellate Court affirming the order passed by the trial Court whereby his application under Order 39 Rule 1 & 2 of the CPC for issuance of temporary injunction has been rejected.

2. As per plaintiff, he has instituted a civil suit before the trial Court for declaration of his title to the suit land and for permanent injunction restraining the defendant from interfering with his possession over the same.
He has submitted that he is the owner of the suit land and there has never been any passage through the same leading to any other land.
The defendant No.1 was the owner of adjacent land which has been acquired by defendant No.5 under the provisions of Land Acquisition Act and compensation for the land was paid to her.
Thereafter defendant No.1 was left with land bearing survey No.458 area 0.247 hectare.
She was always aware that after acquisition no land would be left for her to approach her land.
3 . It is further submitted that defendant No.1 filed an application under Section 131 of M.P. Land Revenue Code, 1959 against defendant No.4 for grant of passage to her for approaching her land.
The plaintiff was not made a party in those proceedings and was not heard.
By order dated 09.03.2018 the Tehsildar held that defendant No.1 is entitled to go to her land through the lands of the neighboring agriculturist including the plaintiff.
The plaintiff preferred an appeal under Section 44(1) of the Code, 1959 which was dismissed by the Sub Divisional Officer by order dated 18.04.2019.
Thus, apprehending threat to possession over the suit land from defendant No.1 the suit was filed.

Along with the plaint an application under Order 39 Rule 1 & 2 CPC was also filed by plaintiff for issuance of temporary injunction restraining defendant No.1 from forcibly dispossessing him from the suit land and taking possession thereof.

The application was contested by defendant No.1.
4.

The Courts below have rejected plaintiff's application for issuance of temporary injunction despite finding prima facie case in his favour but upon recording a finding to the effect that balance of convenience and irreparable injury is not in his favour as defendant No.1 being the owner of her land is entitled to go to her land through the land of adjoining agriculturists, hence order has rightly been passed by the revenue authority on application under Section 131 of the Code, 1959 filed by her.
5.
I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and have considered their rival submissions.

2

6. Section 131 of the M.P. Land Revenue Code reads as under:
[131. Rights of way and other private easements.

- (1) In the event of a dispute arising as to the route by which a cultivator shall have access to his fields or to the waste or pasture lands of the village, otherwise than by the recognised roads, paths or common land, including those road and paths recorded in the village Wajib-ul-arz prepared unde r section 242 or as to the source from or course by which he may avail himself of water, a Tahsildar may, after local enquiry, decide, the matter with reference to the previous custom in each case and with due regard to the conveniences of all the parties concerned.
(2) No order passed under this section shall debar any person from establishing such rights of easement as he may claim by a civil suit."

Section 135 of the Code, 1959 reads as under:
"135. Acquisition of land for road, paths, etc. - (1) If, on the application of the villagers or otherwise, the Collector is, after enquiry satisfied that it is expedient to acquire any land for the purpose of providing a road not exceeding ten feet in width cart track or path for the use of the village community in such village he may call upon the residents of the village to deposit the amount of compensation, payable in respect of such land under sub- section (3) within a specified period.

On such deposit being made the Collector may, by order published in the prescribed manner, acquire such land and upon the making of such order, such land shall vest absolutely in the State Government.

(2) Any person claiming any interest in any such land may within period of one year from the date of vesting under sub-section (1) make an application to the Collector for compensation in respect of his interest.

(3) The compensation payable in respect of such land shall be fifteen times the land revenue assessed or assessable thereon."
7. From a perusal of the aforesaid provisions it is clear that there should be existence of a customary way for grant of a right of way.
In absence of any such custom, the agriculturist can be permitted to go through the land of any other agriculturist provided that the same is legally acquired by the competent authority.
In the present matter, there is no customary way for the plaintiff to go to her land.
On the contrary, in her application under Section 131 of the Code, 1959 the defendant No.1 had herself pleaded that since 2009 she is not having any access to go to her land.

It is evident that the said position has been in existence since 2009 and it is not a case where the existing right of way to land of defendant No.1 has been obstructed by any agriculturist including the plaintiff.
8.

In the proceeding under Section 131 of the Code, 1959 admittedly plaintiff was not impleaded as a party and no notice of hearing was issued to him and no opportunity was afforded to him prior to passing of the order therein.

The right of way through the land of plaintiff has been created without any lawful acquisition of his land and in fact a new way has been directed to be created which is Mahesh vs Jamilabai on 12 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148203953/
3 impermissible.

While it is true that a right of way can be granted looking to the convenience of the party as per Section 131, but the same can also be done only by following the procedure as prescribed under Section 135 of the Code, 1959.
The same has not been done in the matter.
9. The title of plaintiff to his land has been upheld and prima facie case has been found in his favour.
It is also evident that as of now there is no way existing over plaintiff's land and a new status has been directed to be created.
The primary purpose of an injunction application is for maintaining the status as was existing on the date of filing of the suit which ought to have been done by the Courts below.
The balance of convenience was thus in directing maintenance of status as it existing on the date of filing of the suit.

Since defendant No.1 has not been using the land of plaintiff ever since 2009 no irreparable injury would be caused to her if the said state of affairs is directed to be continued and on the contrary plaintiff would suffer irreparable loss in case injunction is not granted in his favour.
10. Thus, in my opinion, the impugned orders passed by the Courts b elo w cannot be sustained and are hereby set aside.
The injunction application filed by the plaintiff stands allowed.
No costs.

(PRANAY VERMA) JUDGE jyoti Mahesh vs Jamilabai on 12 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148203953/
